visuals.title: Paper at a glance
visuals.purpose: What problem does the paper tackle, what is the idea, and what did it achieve?
visuals.alt_text: Five boxes left to right: problem (RNNs are sequential), idea (attention only), how (multi-head self-attention plus positional encoding), result (28.4 and 41.8 BLEU), limits (quadratic cost, added position).

visuals.title: How the Transformer works
visuals.purpose: What are the parts of the model and how does data flow from input tokens to next-token probabilities?
visuals.alt_text: Encoder column: embedding plus position, then six layers of self-attention and feed-forward. Decoder column: masked self-attention, encoder-decoder attention fed by the encoder, feed-forward, then linear and softmax to probabilities.

visuals.title: The main result: English-German BLEU
visuals.purpose: How does the Transformer's translation score compare with earlier models and ensembles?
visuals.alt_text: Horizontal bar chart of EN-DE BLEU. Earlier models from 23.75 (ByteNet) to 26.36 (ConvS2S ensemble). Transformer base 27.3, Transformer big 28.4.

visuals.title: Reading Figure 1 step by step
visuals.purpose: In what order should you read the architecture figure, and what does each part do?
visuals.alt_text: The architecture figure redrawn with five numbered callouts: embeddings and position, encoder layer, masked decoder self-attention, encoder-decoder attention, output projection.

visuals.title: Scaled dot-product attention
visuals.purpose: What goes into one attention operation, what happens inside, and what comes out?
visuals.alt_text: Q and K go into a matrix multiply, then scale by one over root d_k, optional mask, softmax; the resulting weights multiply V to give the output.

visuals.title: Multi-head attention
visuals.purpose: How do several attention heads run side by side and get combined?
visuals.alt_text: Q, K, V each projected h = 8 times to 64 dimensions, attention run in each head in parallel, outputs concatenated and projected back to 512.

visuals.title: Positional encoding
visuals.purpose: How does the model learn word order when nothing in it is sequential?
visuals.alt_text: Token embedding plus a sinusoidal position vector of the same size gives the input to the first layer. Each dimension is a sine or cosine of a different frequency.

visuals.title: What changed: recurrence vs self-attention
visuals.purpose: How does a self-attention layer differ from a recurrent or convolutional layer in parallelism and path length?
visuals.alt_text: Side by side: recurrent layer passes a state step by step (O(n) sequential steps, O(n) path); self-attention links every pair directly (O(1) steps, O(1) path) at O(n squared times d) cost.

visuals.title: Decoding Equation 1
visuals.purpose: What does each symbol in the attention equation mean?
visuals.alt_text: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K-transpose over root d_k) V, with each symbol labelled in words and a one-line plain reading.

visuals.title: How the ideas connect
visuals.purpose: How do the paper's main terms relate to each other?
visuals.alt_text: Concept map linking Transformer, encoder, decoder, multi-head attention, scaled dot-product attention, query/key/value, masking, positional encoding, feed-forward, residual and layer norm.

visuals.title: Where it breaks
visuals.purpose: What limits and assumptions does the paper itself state?
visuals.alt_text: Coral boxes: cost grows with sequence length squared; restricted attention trades path length; averaging lowers resolution; position must be injected; extrapolation is untested; results are translation and parsing only.

visuals.title: What it builds on
visuals.purpose: Which earlier work does the Transformer combine, and what role does each play?
visuals.alt_text: Left to right: seq2seq and attention foundations, ResNet and LayerNorm methods used, ByteNet and ConvS2S baselines, leading to the Transformer.

visuals.title: Predict: dev BLEU vs number of heads
visuals.purpose: Before reading Table 3, what do you expect happens to quality as you split attention into more, smaller heads?
visuals.alt_text: Empty bar chart with five slots for 1, 4, 8, 16 and 32 heads, each with a question mark, y-axis dev BLEU from 0 to 30.

visuals.title: Dev BLEU vs number of heads
visuals.purpose: What did Table 3 rows (A) actually show about the number of heads?
visuals.alt_text: Bar chart of dev BLEU: 1 head 24.9, 4 heads 25.5, 8 heads 25.8, 16 heads 25.8, 32 heads 25.4.

visuals.title: Original Figure 1: The Transformer architecture
visuals.purpose: What does the authors' own architecture diagram look like, so you can check the v02 and v04 redraws against it?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's original architecture diagram: encoder stack on the left, decoder stack on the right, with Add & Norm, attention and feed-forward blocks, embeddings, positional encoding, linear and softmax.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Fig. 1, p. 3, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Figure 2 (left): Scaled Dot-Product Attention
visuals.purpose: What does the authors' diagram of one attention operation look like, to check against v05a?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's original diagram: Q and K into MatMul, then Scale, optional Mask, SoftMax, then MatMul with V.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Fig. 2, p. 4, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Figure 2 (right): Multi-Head Attention
visuals.purpose: What does the authors' multi-head diagram look like, to check against v05b?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's original diagram: V, K, Q each through stacked Linear layers, h parallel Scaled Dot-Product Attention blocks, Concat, then Linear.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Fig. 2, p. 4, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Table 1: cost, sequential steps and path length
visuals.purpose: What exactly does Table 1 compare across layer types?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's Table 1: complexity per layer, sequential operations and maximum path length for self-attention, recurrent, convolutional and restricted self-attention layers.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Table 1, p. 6, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Table 2: translation results
visuals.purpose: How do the Transformer's BLEU scores and training costs compare with earlier models?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's Table 2: BLEU on EN-DE and EN-FR and training cost in FLOPs for earlier models, ensembles and both Transformer sizes.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Table 2, p. 8, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Table 3: model variations
visuals.purpose: What happens when each part of the base model is changed?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's Table 3: rows A to E and big, varying heads, key size, model size, dropout, label smoothing and positional encoding, with dev perplexity, BLEU and parameters.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Table 3, p. 9, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Table 4: English constituency parsing
visuals.purpose: How does the Transformer do on parsing compared with other parsers?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's Table 4: WSJ section 23 F1 for parsers trained on WSJ only, semi-supervised, multi-task and generative settings, including the 4-layer Transformer.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Table 4, p. 10, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Figure 3: following a long-distance link
visuals.purpose: What does one attention head look at when it reads the word 'making'?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's Figure 3, rotated to read left to right: encoder self-attention in layer 5 linking 'making' to 'more difficult'; colours are different heads.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Fig. 3, p. 13, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Figure 4: heads that resolve 'its'
visuals.purpose: Which words do two attention heads link to the pronoun 'its'?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's Figure 4, rotated: left, isolated attention from 'its' for heads 5 and 6; right, full attention of head 5. Both are encoder layer 5.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Fig. 4, p. 14, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Original Figure 5: heads with different jobs
visuals.purpose: Do different attention heads behave differently?
visuals.alt_text: The paper's Figure 5, rotated: two encoder heads in layer 5 with different attention patterns that seem to follow sentence structure.
visuals.credit: Reproduced from Vaswani et al. (2017), Fig. 5, p. 15, under the permission stated on p. 1 for scholarly use with attribution.

visuals.title: Telephone game vs group chat
visuals.purpose: What is the core idea, in one everyday picture?
visuals.alt_text: Left: children passing a message down a line. Right: everyone in one group chat. Labels: old way, new way.

visuals.title: What the paper did
visuals.purpose: What did the authors do, in three steps?
visuals.alt_text: Three panels: old models read one word at a time; the new model lets all words look at each other; it translated better and trained faster.

visuals.title: Building blocks, bottom to top
visuals.purpose: What do you need to understand first, and what builds on it?
visuals.alt_text: Stacked blocks from bottom: words as number lists, matching scores, weights that add to one, attention, many heads, the full Transformer.

visuals.alt_text: Chain of hidden states h1, h2, h3 with the arrow between them labelled with a question mark.
